parameters.content:
# Invoice intake
**Fetch → store → label → hand over.** Nothing here can fail after the mailbox marks an email as read: it is stored in Postgres first. Then each email runs on its own in 'Process Email' (own log, isolated failures; a resend in the same batch is still a duplicate). No AI here: the guardrail sits in front of the AI, on the exact text it reads, including PDFs.

**Mailbox (set up by Hallmann IT).** A dedicated invoice mailbox that receives nothing else; colleagues forward invoices there. The mailbox boundary is the access control: a token for it can never see anyone else's mail.

**IMAP** works with any server (Exchange, M365, the demo mailbox). **Gmail**: credential with Custom Scopes = gmail.modify only (read + label; the workflow has no send or delete node); production: Workspace service account approved by the admin for this one mailbox. Enable Gmail, disable IMAP: same pipeline.

parameters.query: insert into inbound_emails (message_id, received_at, from_addr, subject, body, body_hash, attachments, meta) values ($1, $2::timestamptz, $3, $4, $5, $6, $7::jsonb, $8::jsonb) on conflict (message_id) do nothing returning message_id

insert into attachments (message_id, name, mime, size_bytes, sha256, content) select $1, f->>'name', f->>'mime', length(decode(f->>'b64', 'base64')), encode(sha256(decode(f->>'b64', 'base64')), 'hex'), decode(f->>'b64', 'base64') from jsonb_array_elements($2::jsonb) f on conflict (message_id, name) do nothing returning name
